conviction_note: The findings sum to a small positive (+0.6): revenue tailwinds from Novo's cash-pay pill quarter, the Lilly deal and the peptide policy, plus a crowded short, against the arithmetic of a Q4 EBITDA ramp that the FY guide requires after two cuts. The name has fallen after 6 of its last 7 prints and the options pay for upside, so p_up stays at 50 and the scaled number is 0 on a move of about 14 points either way. The gap between the sum and the scaled number is the reaction function vetoing a modest revenue read.
bar: Q3 revenue: company guide $880-900m and adj EBITDA $75-95m (Q2 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000161/hims-20260630x8xkearningsr.htm). Consensus revenue $893.4m (Zacks, https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:ebe0b56bc094b:0-hims-q3-earnings-can-weight-loss-momentum-drive-performance/) and $892.7m (Benzinga), which agree. EPS $0.06 (Benzinga/Chartmill) to $0.07 (Zacks), whisper $0.09 (finviz/Earnings Whispers https://finviz.com/news/413815/hims-hers-must-prove-its-weight-loss-revenue-surge-can-coexist-with-cash-and-margins). FY2026 guide: revenue $3.1-3.3bn, adj EBITDA $275-325m.
positioning_check: Short interest about 23% of float per a Benzinga piece of Nov 2026 (https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63020607/hims-hers-short-interest-climbs-to-23-ahead-of-earnings-can-the-stock-break-out, headline only, page 403). Trade-Ideas showed about 27% on 2026-10-21 (https://www.trade-ideas.com/stock-info/HIMS/). FINRA 2026-08-14 settlement: 58.7m shares and 4.5 days to cover (curvedtrading via search snippet). MarketBeat had 63.4m shares, 31.5% of float, on 2026-05-15. That is a crowded short with about 4 days to cover. Options: 25-delta skew -14.56 vol points, so calls are bid over puts ('upside paid'); put/call open interest 0.32; event-implied move 13.72%. Tape: -23.8% over 20 days and -7.5% over 5 days. Part of that is macro: on 2026-11-05 the Nasdaq fell 5.4% (https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/nasdaq-enters-correction-as-ai-stocks-sink-after-midterm-elections/268903) and HIMS fell 9.75%. Beta is 2.53.

findings.finding: Novo Nordisk's Q3 (reported 2026-11-04, after Hims last spoke on 08-10): Wegovy pill sales of DKK 5.4bn in the quarter, 8m+ US prescriptions, ~80% of new-to-brand scripts and roughly 90% cash-pay. Combined US Wegovy rose 21% while the injectable fell 13%. That is the channel Hims sells the Wegovy pill through since its March 2026 Novo deal. It supports Hims' US weight-loss revenue at or above the top of the $880-900m guide, against a $893m consensus already near the top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not paid: in Q2 2026 revenue beat by ~4.3% and the stock fell 3.97% on a margin/EPS miss. In Q1 2026 revenue missed and the stock fell 14.1%. Six of the last 7 prints were down.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue consensus has already been revised up ~15% in three months (Chartmill) and sits near the top of the guide, so most of this is in the bar. What remains is the size of a beat above $900m. If the market had priced a large beat, the 20-day tape would not be -24% into the print. The macro crash on 11-05 confounds that reading.
findings.independence: The Lilly Q3 (2026-10-30) also showed strong demand: US Zepbound +48%, Foundayo new starts doubled sequentially, net price -15% (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3018734/lly-stock-jumps-as-q3-earnings-beat-estimates-2026-sales-view-raised). The Novo self-pay subscription plans that Hims was due to join (https://pharmaphorum.com/news/novo-hits-back-rivals-cut-price-wegovy-subscriptions, 2026-03-31) are the channel. Both are proxies, not Hims numbers.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-06 Lilly and Hims announced that Zepbound ($299+/mo) and Foundayo ($149+/mo) will be sold on the Hims platform at LillyDirect self-pay prices, with Hims committing never to compound Lilly GLP-1s. This came after the Q3 guide was set, so it is new input to the Q4/FY2026 revenue guide given on this call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY revenue guide raises have not been rewarded when EBITDA was trimmed: Aug 2026 revenue guide raised from $2.8-3.0bn to $3.1-3.3bn with the EBITDA top cut, stock -3.97%. May 2026 revenue raised, EBITDA cut, stock -14.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal itself is priced: +8.1% on 11-06 (https://www.trefis.com/stock/hims/articles/623742/what-sent-hims-hers-stock-higher/2026-11-08), then -6.6% to -7.3% on 11-09 before the print. What is not priced is how management turns it into Q4 revenue and subscriber guidance, which no estimate can yet carry. At self-pay prices the margin contribution is probably thin, which caps the size.
findings.independence: Pharmexec (https://www.pharmexec.com/view/hims-hers-partners-eli-lilly-sell-obesity-medicines, 2026-11-06) reports the same deal. Lilly's Q3 Foundayo traction (new starts doubled, ~4 in 10 oral starts) is a different source pointing to demand for the added products.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-28/30 HHS published an interim enforcement-discretion policy allowing 503A compounding of six peptides, including BPC-157. Hims had already secured a California peptide facility and tested ingredients; the CEO said it could 'move extremely quickly'. This is the first call since, and a launch timeline or a Q4/2027 contribution may be given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior print with a new-category regulatory unlock. The stock rose ~5% on the HHS news on 10-28 and ~6% on the 10-15 report of the policy, then gave it all back.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline was bought and then fully sold: the stock went from ~$28 on 10-28 to $23.36 now. So the market is not carrying a peptide revenue line, and an actual launch date plus pricing on the call is incremental. Against that, the policy is a non-binding draft (Venable) and the 11-03 midterm result may cloud HHS deregulation, so the size stays small.
findings.independence: Venable (https://www.venable.com/insights/publications/2026/11/hhs-announces-interim-enforcement) and RAPS (https://www.raps.org/resource/hhs-will-permit-compounding-of-six-peptides-ahead-of-formal-rulemaking.html, 2026-10-29) confirm the policy. The Hims readiness comes from the TIKR summary of the Aug call (https://www.tikr.com/blog/hims-hers-stock-has-barely-moved-since-its-biggest-mens-health-launch-heres-what-november-9-has-to-show).

findings.finding: Guide arithmetic: FY2026 adj EBITDA $275-325m less Q1 $44.3m, Q2 $60.3m and the Q3 guide of $75-95m leaves Q4 needing about $110m at the midpoints. That is ~11.5% on ~$950m of implied Q4 revenue, against an 8% margin in Q2 and 9-11% guided for Q3. Branded GLP-1 mix (now adding Lilly at self-pay prices), international spend, injectable testosterone and a peptide build all pressure gross margin, which fell from 76% to 64% year on year. The FY EBITDA guide has been cut twice in 2026, and the margin line is the one this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITDA guide cuts: May 2026 FY EBITDA cut from $300-375m to $275-350m, stock -14.1%. Aug 2026 top cut to $325m with Q2 GM 64% and an EPS miss, stock -3.97% (Zacks headline 'plunges post Q2 miss, gross margin down'). Feb 2025, -22.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The previews (finviz/Earnings Whispers) frame the risk as a Q3 margin near 8%, not as the Q4 step-up that the unchanged FY range requires. If the market priced a third cut, the skew would be put-bid; it is call-bid at -14.6 vol points. Against that, a 24% drawdown and 23-32% short interest mean part of a cut is likely already expected, so the negative is shrunk.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001773751/000177375126000074/hims-20260331x8xkearningsr.htm) gives Q1 adj EBITDA of $44.3m. The finviz preview says management expects EBITDA margin to climb toward ~12% by Q4. Both are company documents; the arithmetic is mine.

findings.finding: Positioning: about 23% of float short (Benzinga, Nov 2026) and ~27% per Trade-Ideas on 10-21, with ~4 days to cover. Calls are bid over puts (skew -14.56, put/call OI 0.32). The stock is -23.8% over 20 days, partly on the 11-05 Nasdaq -5.4% macro crash rather than company news. A clean margin print has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2025 was the one up print (+18.1%) and came with record short interest. Otherwise heavy short interest has not stopped declines (Q1 2026 -14.1% with record shorts per Stocktwits).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own state, not information it lacks. It shapes the asymmetry of the reaction: a crowded short into a washed-out tape makes a relief rally more violent than the symmetric implied move suggests. The call-side skew says the option market already sees part of this.
findings.independence: Trade-Ideas (https://www.trade-ideas.com/stock-info/HIMS/, 2026-10-21), the macro crash (https://www.investmentnews.com/equities/nasdaq-enters-correction-as-ai-stocks-sink-after-midterm-elections/268903, 2026-11-05) and the baseline skew.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows receivables rising from $32.1m to $375.3m, of which $347.4m are manufacturer discount/rebate receivables tied to branded GLP-1 supply. A $329m receivables build was largely offset by a $324m rise in payables; Q2 FCF was -$68m, and a ~$400m receivables facility plus >$400m of converts were added. Q3 cash flow is likely negative again as branded volume grows. The money funds a corroborated revenue ramp (+38% in Q2, guide +47-50%), so this is a cash-quality talking point rather than distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 was the first negative-FCF print (-$68m), with the stock -3.97%. There is no earlier instance.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed and discussed in previews ('continued cash burn' per Earnings Whispers), so it is largely priced. The residual is whether Q3 OCF is worse than Q2's -$36m. Answer to the financing question: the money buys branded drug working capital for visible demand, so the sign is near zero.
findings.independence: finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/413815/hims-hers-must-prove-its-weight-loss-revenue-surge-can-coexist-with-cash-and-margins) on the receivables facility and the converts. It is the same underlying disclosure, so not fully independent.

findings.finding: The FTC, California and Utah lawsuit (filed 2026-07-29) targets collecting billing details before a provider consultation and a hidden cancel path. Any Q3 changes to intake or cancellation flows would hit conversion and churn in the quarter being reported. No change is confirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell ~12-15% on 07-29 on the filing. The Q2 print on 08-10 (-3.97%) came after it.
findings.why_not_priced: The lawsuit is priced. The quarter-level effect on subscriber adds (Q2 +307k) is not visible until the print. This is an inference with no document showing changed flows, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Alston & Bird advisory (https://www.alston.com/en/insights/publications/2026/08/ftc-lawsuit-hims-hers-rosca), same lawsuit. Nothing independent shows a subscriber impact.

findings.finding: The DEA telemedicine flexibilities for Schedule III drugs (testosterone, Hims' fastest-growing specialty after weight loss, with injectable TRT launched 2026-10-21) expire 2026-12-31 with no permanent rule public. The call is the first chance for management to say how it prescribes after that date, and the August call did not address it.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits under 3% of next-12-month revenue (TIKR), so it is small, and the past pattern is extensions granted at the last minute. Commentary on the call is inside the window; the rule itself resolves after it.

findings.finding: Democrats won both chambers in the 2026-11-03 midterms. That may raise scrutiny of HHS deregulation (peptides) and telehealth compounding in 2027, which could colour how investors read Hims' new-category guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: This is macro-to-company transmission that no counterparty has confirmed. A proxy only.

findings.finding: Insiders sold 133,905 shares (~$3.8m) over the last quarter under 10b5-1 plans, including Soleil Boughton 3,462 shares at $27.60 on 2026-10-28 and COO Michael Chi 14,027 at $28.39 on 2026-09-15. There were no insider buys at the lows.
findings.why_not_priced: These are small scheduled 10b5-1 sales, routine for the name and largely uninformative.

outside_window.finding: The DEA permanent telemedicine registration rule, or a fifth extension, decides post-2026 testosterone prescribing; the date is 2026-12-31.
Novo's ~50% Wegovy US list-price cut from 2027-01-01 may change self-pay economics on Hims' branded weight-loss line.

baseline_tension: The call-bid skew (-14.6) and a crowded short agree with my small positives on revenue and positioning; the -24% run-up is mostly macro. The reaction history (6 of 7 prints down, the stock trading on margin) and the Q4 EBITDA ramp arithmetic cut against the skew, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells prints, 6 of 7 down): the Novo cash-pay revenue tailwind cut from +0.8 to +0.5.
Rule 7 (crowded short at ~23-32% of float, calls bid): the Q4 EBITDA-ramp negative shrunk from -1.5 to -1.2, keeping it only because the guide arithmetic is the stated reason the skew may be wrong.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the receivables facility and converts fund branded-drug working capital for a corroborated +38-50% revenue ramp, so that finding went from -0.4 to -0.2.
Rule 6 (keep inside the window): the DEA rule date moved to outside_window; only the in-window call commentary stays, cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is small): the midterm finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
p_up, abs_move_pct and print_vs_bar were left unchanged.
